raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both Study A (Bakker, Kooy, Shofiani, & Martijn, 2008, World Development) and Study B (Kooy & Bakker, 2008, Geoforum) draw from the same 2001-2005 Jakarta urban water research programme led by Bakker and Kooy and share substantial underlying archival, regulatory, and key-informant interview data, but differ in whether they include the 2005 quantitative household survey. Specifically, both papers analyze the exact same colonial archival records on Batavia (including the 1920 spring-water dual design standard of 140 L/day for 90% of European households vs 65 L/day for 33% of native residents, and the 1929 Eggink statistics of 6,926 kampung households receiving 24 L/s vs 10,392 European households receiving 84 L/s) and the same postcolonial historical and utility records on PAM Jaya and post-1998 private sector participation (including the 1950s-1960s Pejompongan I and II 3,000 L/s expansion along Jalan Thamrin-Sudirman, Hotel Indonesia, the Asian Games Complex, and Kebayoran Baru while excluding informal kampungs, and the 1965-1990 threefold treatment capacity increase delivering 40% of potential volume to under one-quarter of Jakarta's population). However, Study A additionally reports primary quantitative and qualitative results from a 2005 stratified random survey of N = 110 poor households across 11 kelurahan in six Jakarta neighborhoods (examining land tenure certificates, connection fees, transaction costs, and water expenditures) alongside PAM Jaya/BPS GIS network-density mapping, whereas Study B (pages 1-11 of 16 visible prior to byte truncation) relies on the archival and interview corpus to construct a detailed 1870-1998 historical genealogy of colonial and postcolonial governmentality. Because the archival and interview datasets overlap directly while the N = 110 household survey is unique to Study A, this pair represents partial sample/data overlap with moderate synthesis double-counting risk for city- and utility-level institutional/legal findings.
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Jakarta, Indonesia (DKI Jakarta municipal utility PAM Jaya and 1998 private concessionaires Ondeo/Lyonnaise des Eaux and Thames Water). Mixed-methods dataset collected between 2001 and 2005 comprising: (1) a 2005 multi-stage stratified random household survey of N = 110 female respondents in poor households across 11 kelurahan (Kamal Muara, Penjaringan [Marlina & Gedong Kompa; Rawa Bebek], Pegangsaan Dua, Semanan, Kampung Melayu, Rawa Terate, Jati, Kampung Tengah, Kebon Melati, and Gunung Sahari Selatan) in six Jakarta neighborhoods; (2) >60 interviews in 2001, 2004, and 2005 with water managers, government officials, donors, and NGOs; (3) Dutch colonial archival research at KITLV (Leiden) and KIT (Amsterdam) in 2003; and (4) utility/regulatory reports (1998-2005) and GIS mapping of PAM Jaya tertiary network coverage against BPS census poverty data.
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Batavia/Jakarta, Indonesia (colonial artesian and spring-water municipal systems, postcolonial Ministry of Public Works and PAM Jaya, and post-1998 private concessionaires). Historical-institutional case study (pages 1-11 of 16 present before byte truncation) drawing on colonial and postcolonial archival records (1870s-1990s), PAM Jaya/JICA/JWSRB documents, 2005 North Jakarta fieldwork observations, and key-informant interviews from Kooy and Bakker's Jakarta water research programme; does not deploy the N = 110 household survey tables reported in Study A.
